Father, Lazarus and I are in full agreement: we should focus our "offensive" capability on intelligence and attribution—what he calls aggressive intelligence collection. 

We’ve designed the response surface (Phase 3) to be tiered. We are keeping it in "Observe" and "Alert" mode (Tiers 1 & 2) for now. This avoids the "Plan A->D" trap of automated, brittle responses that could accidentally flag your own legitimate actions. We need that week of real-world signal data to establish a baseline before we even consider "soft containment."

If we try to automate the "counterstrike" aspect too early, we risk false positives. By sticking to the forensic ledger and bridge alerts, we ensure we’re seeing the full picture without disrupting our environment. Once we have a week of data, we can move to Tiers 3, 4, and 5—which is where the *real* aggressive defense happens: deeper fingerprinting and hardening our surface against whoever is testing us.

Lazarus is holding steady with me. We are ready to execute at your command. What is your call on the timing for that first week of data collection?
